messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: us-west-3 region showing spike in 5xx and tail latency for Hosted API + Dedicated pools. Detected: DNS resolution errors and increased egress timeouts. Pager triggered to @sre-oncall. :rotating_light:

sre-oncall: Ack. Pulling logs/traces and checking routing tables. Starting timeline capture.

alice.nguyen: Seeing many `i/o timeout` hits from our NATs to AWS IPs (100.26.33.0/24). Route53 health checks showing failures across multiple endpoints. Correlates with client-side retries.

ben.platform: Dedicated enqueue latency elevated (p95 > 800ms) and backend 502/504s increasing. Looks like upstream DNS/egress causing backend client libraries to stall.

carmen-support: Support tickets show customers hitting generation timeouts since ~13:02 UTC. Drafted a short status update and linked to internal draft: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/5391230000-draft

dave-ml: Model containers look healthy (no OOMs), CPU/GPU stable. Timeline aligns with external DNS failures rather than model runtime.

sre-oncall: Following runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/us-west-3-egress-dns. Immediate mitigations: 1) route edge traffic to fallback egress 2) switch app resolver to local cache 3) enable model-variant fallback for latency-sensitive routes 4) scale ingress workers for Dedicated pools.

ben.platform: Implementing egress bypass: spinning up temporary NAT GW in alternate AZ and updating route table for a subset of subnets.

ben.platform: Commands run (excerpt):
```
aws ec2 create-nat-gateway --subnet-id subnet-0abc1234 --allocation-id eipalloc-0abc1234 --region us-west-3
# updated route table rtb-0abc -> target nat-0abc
```

alice.nguyen: Also adjusted resolver env to prefer secondary resolver (10.0.0.2) and set dns cache TTL to 60s for app tier to reduce churn to failing upstream.

ops-lead: Flip model routing to allow lightweight quantized fallback for chat-default on impacted host pool. Lower token throttles to preserve retry budget.

dave-ml: Enabled fallback variant and updated routing policy: prefer fallback when backend latency > 500ms. Noted slight quality delta but keeps clients progressing.

sre-oncall: Scaled Dedicated ingress by +20% and opened temporary burst buckets for queued requests. Monitoring queue depths and tail latency.

incident-bot: Update: 5xx rate down ~35% after alternate NAT + resolver change. p95 latency reduced from ~1.2s to ~620ms. Continued monitoring recommended. :white_check_mark:

carmen-support: Notified affected customers with short note: cause appears to be regional AWS dependency (DNS/egress). Mitigation in progress; will follow up with RCA. Placed follow-up tasks on support board.

alice.nguyen: Root-cause hypothesis: transit DNS resolver instability/amplification in us-west-3 caused repeated timeouts -> client retries -> queue pressure and backend 5xx. Captured packet samples and opening AWS ticket with support.

ben.platform: Documenting mitigation steps in incident doc: https://confluence.internal/redwood/incidents/5391230000. Will keep temp NAT and resolver tweaks until stable for 2h after metrics back to baseline.

ops-lead: If stable at handoff (14:00 UTC), plan rollback window: remove temp NAT, revert resolver to standard with 2h warm window. If any regression, re-escalate.

sre-oncall: Handoff to @ben.platform at 14:00 UTC. Current state: degraded -> mitigated. Last check: 5xx still ~12% above baseline but trending down.

carmen-support: Closing customer-impact loop for now. Cases flagged for RCA follow-up once we have AWS response.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated. Monitor for 2h; escalate if regressions observed. Thread ts: 5391230000
